newsitem.title: FRANCE: Canal says GBL stake "too little/too much".
newsitem.headline: Canal says GBL stake "too little/too much".

text.p: A 1.33 percent stake acquired in French pay-television company Canal Plus by Groupe Bruxelles Lambert (GBL) was either "too much or too little," Canal Plus director Laurent Perpere said on Wednesday.
GBL, headed by Belgian businessman Albert Frere, last Friday bought the Canal Plus stake from Paribas.
Canal Plus chairman Pierre Lescure told an analysts meeting that "Frere must regret not getting into Canalsatellite," when he was invited to.

Lescure, asked about the possibility that GBL might have bought the stake and was holding it on behalf of Cie Generale des Eaux, as had been rumoured in the market, said, "It's not news that Albert Frere and Generale des Eaux are on good terms." But he added that any carrying of stock would be a problem for Canal Plus' shareholder agreement.
Generale des Eaux is one of Canal Plus' group of stable shareholders, along with Havas and Societe Generale.

GBL director Didier Belens told French business newspaper Les Echos in an interview published on Monday that just because the Belgian company was a major shareholder in Luxembourg broadcaster CLT, did not rule out an investment in digital television on its own.
Canal Plus recently launched its Canalsatellite digital service which is the first European digital television operation.
Cie Luxembourgeoise de Telediffusion (CLT) last week dropped plans to launch a German digital television service planned with Bertelsmann AG. CLT is controlled by Luxembourg's Audiofina.
